acceptance: A test shows `.filter(col > k).n_unique()` on DataFusion equals the Polars and SQL answer, failing before the fix.
Every aggregate method on UnifiedExpr is either implemented on the deferred filter or raises on DataFusion; a test enumerates them.
The list of DataFrame queries using `.filter(...)` before an aggregate, and whether each answer changed, is recorded here.
context: FINAL 2026-11-15. PR #4256 merged as ebaccea2ca. UnifiedExpr has 13 aggregate terminals; the DataFusion deferred filter handled 5 (sum, count, mean/avg, min, max) and the other 8 (first, last, std, var, quantile, n_unique, approx_n_unique) silently dropped the condition (filter(x>50).n_unique() returned 8; correct answer 3). Now: sum/mean/count/min/max/std/first/last use DataFusion `filter=`; n_unique uses count(distinct, filter=) and still skips NULL; approx_n_unique uses approx_distinct(filter=); var/quantile use CASE WHEN inside the aggregate (DataFusion 55 cannot plan the filtered form). Every other method/operator/property on a filtered expression raises NotImplementedError (incl. native, double filter, use as operand/argument; reviewer-found gap closed). Query audit (AST search over all DataFrame query modules): only sum/count follow an expression .filter( (TPC-H Q8/Q12/Q14 forms, TPC-Havoc Q8/Q12/Q14, read primitives); optimized logical plans identical before/after, so no answer or timing changed (not re-run on data). Tests: test_datafusion_deferred_filter.py 17 passing, compares every exact aggregate with Polars on grouped data and enumerates UnifiedExpr methods; preflight 1743 passed; fail-before shown by stand-in (8 vs 3), new tests not run against old code. Notes: ungrouped var/quantile via select fail in DataFusion 55 regardless of filter; grouped filtered n_unique keeps the single-stage distinct plan (possible perf gap on high-cardinality groups, not correctness).
description:
Correctness defect found while removing the redundant Q28 filter (PR #4239). In `benchbox/platforms/dataframe/unified_frame.py` the DataFusion path wraps `expr.filter(cond)` in `_DataFusionDeferredFilter`, which has no `n_unique`. The call falls through to the unfiltered `UnifiedExpr.n_unique()`, so the condition is dropped: TPC-DS Q28's old `col("ss_list_price").filter(is_not_null()).n_unique()` produced the same plan as plain `n_unique()` (logical 40 nodes, physical 46). For Q28 the answer was right only because `n_unique()` already skips NULL. Any `.filter(cond)` with another condition followed by an aggregate the deferred wrapper does not implement would return a wrong answer on DataFusion with no error.

Expected: every aggregate reachable after `.filter(...)` on DataFusion either applies the filter (e.g. `count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN cond THEN x END)` or the DataFusion aggregate FILTER clause) or raises; no silent fall-through. Audit which aggregates the wrapper implements against those UnifiedExpr exposes, and grep DataFrame query modules (TPC-H, TPC-DS, read primitives, others) for `.filter(` followed by an aggregate to find affected queries.

Guardrails: a query whose answer changes is a defect fix, not a reference update: check it against SQL/other engines. Timed queries touched follow the 10% rule with before/after timings.
